*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: c:\Users\linus\git\context-engine\tmp\test-coverage-audit\04-capture-hook.md
+# Copilot Capture Hook Test-Coverage Audit
+
+Scope: `memory-api/crates/session-api` Copilot capture hook and its immediate
+storage/registration boundary. This audit distinguishes source-backed facts from
+evidence that could not be collected on this host.
+
+## 1. Execution contract (fixture blueprint)
+
+### Invocation and argv
+
+`copilot-capture-hook` accepts only these options ([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L33-L86)):
+
+| Input | Type | Required | Default / behavior |
+|---|---|---:|---|
+| `-h`, `--help` | flag | no | Prints usage and exits zero; implemented as the special `InvalidHookInput("help")` result ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L35-L45)). |
+| `--from-hook-stdin` | flag | no | Reads all stdin as one JSON value. Without it, stdin is not read. |
+| `--transcript-path <PATH>` | path string | yes without `--from-hook-stdin`; otherwise no | The direct-mode absence is an error. In stdin mode, an absent value remains empty and produces a successful skip because the normalized path is not a file ([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L68-L86); [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L56-L64)). |
+| `--store-root <PATH>` | path string | no | Uses this exact root. Otherwise derives a local `.session` root from the working directory, or relative `.session` when no working directory is available ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L370-L381)). |
+| `--workspace-slug <SLUG>` | string | no | `default`. |
+| `--trigger <NAME>` | string | no | `stop`. |
+
+An unknown option and a missing option value are `InvalidHookInput` errors
+([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L41-L65), [args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L199-L205)). On Windows, `/mnt/c/...` and `/c/...` transcript paths are converted to `C:\...`; a drive-letter path should therefore be a fixture case ([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L145-L197)).
+
+### stdin
+
+The hook reads stdin only with `--from-hook-stdin`; `read_to_string` consumes one
+complete UTF-8 stream, then `serde_json::from_str` parses it as `serde_json::Value`
+([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L89-L107)). There is **no deserialization struct**. The effective payload is an object with
+these optional, string-valued aliases:
+
+| JSON field aliases | Effect |
+|---|---|
+| `transcript_path`, `transcriptPath` | Replaces `--transcript-path`. |
+| `workspace_slug`, `workspaceSlug` | Replaces `--workspace-slug`. |
+| `hook_event_name`, `hookEventName` | Replaces `--trigger`; blank or `unknown` normalizes to `stop`. |
+| `tool_use_id`, `toolUseId` | Supplies the full Copilot spill-entry name. |
+| `session_id`, `sessionId` | Supplies the spill-session directory name. |
+| `tool_response`, `toolResponse` | Counts Unicode characters, preserving a present empty string as `Some(0)`. |
+
+The exact extraction is `payload.get(*key)?.as_str().map(str::trim).filter(...)`
+for all but `tool_response` ([args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L108-L142), [args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L157-L177)). Non-string, blank, `"null"`, or missing ordinary fields are ignored; malformed JSON fails. Empty stdin succeeds with CLI/default values.
+
+### Environment
+
+The hook binary has no direct `std::env::var` or `env!` read. It indirectly calls
+`memory_api::workspace::working_dir()` three times. `working_dir()` reads process
+current directory and optional `PWD`; `PWD` affects discovery of the default
+`.session` and `.ticket` roots ([workspace.rs](../../memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs#L108-L113); [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L66-L69), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L85-L100), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L312-L326)). An unavailable current directory does not fail capture by itself.
+
+### Files read
+
+1. The required logical input is the normalized transcript path. The parser opens
+   it with `File::open`, reads it line-by-line as UTF-8 text, skips blank lines,
+   and deserializes each nonblank line as a transcript event ([transcript.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/transcript.rs#L56-L76), [transcript.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/transcript.rs#L124-L144)). The required event shape is JSONL, not a JSON array. A usable transcript needs a session-start event containing `sessionId`/`session_id`/`id` and at least one visible message; otherwise parsing returns `MissingSessionId` or `EmptyTurns` ([transcript.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/transcript.rs#L176-L239)).
+2. For a `tool_use_id` plus `session_id`, the binary derives
+   `<transcript parent>/../chat-session-resources/<session_id>/<tool_use_id>/content.txt`
+   and then `content.json`, retrying five times at 100 ms. It reads raw bytes and
+   uses lossy UTF-8 only to count characters ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L163-L200)).
+3. The transcript tool parser can also extract a spill pointer from event content
+   and read either that direct file or `<pointer>/content.txt`, again as bytes and
+   lossy UTF-8 ([tool_execution.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/tool_execution.rs#L341-L354)).
+4. Before persisting, the store reads existing `session.json`, `transcript.json`,
+   and `events.json` for merge, when present ([store.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store.rs#L787-L815)).
+
+### Files written or mutated
+
+Under `<store-root>/sessions/<session-id>/`, capture creates or merges pretty JSON
+`session.json`, `transcript.json`, and, when events exist, `events.json`. It creates
+or replaces `tool-metrics.json` only when tool-summary data is nonempty, otherwise
+removes that sidecar ([store.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store.rs#L787-L855)). Each JSON write creates parent directories, writes and syncs a UUID-named
+temporary file, then renames it to the destination ([storage.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store/helpers/storage.rs#L94-L146)). The immediate capture path also best-effort writes a store-level metrics rollup, and may best-effort infer worktree/ticket linkage or synthesize follow-up tickets in `.ticket` ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L84-L110), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L300-L367)).
+
+### Exit, stdout, stderr, and lifecycle
+
+Successful capture and intentional missing-transcript skip both print `{}` to
+stdout. A missing transcript also writes `skip: transcript not found ...` to stderr
+and exits zero ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L56-L64), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L109-L113)). Parse/store errors print `[copilot-capture-hook] <error>` to stderr and exit 1. Worktree inference, follow-up ticket synthesis, and rollup errors are explicitly nonfatal ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L35-L45), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L90-L110), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L317-L367)). The hook is therefore fail-closed for its core transcript capture but fail-open for enrichment.
+
+`.github/hooks/hooks.json` invokes `copilot-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin` at
+`UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `SessionEnd`, with `cwd: "."` and
+120-second timeouts ([hooks.json](../../.github/hooks/hooks.json#L3-L9), [hooks.json](../../.github/hooks/hooks.json#L25-L59)). PostToolUse is timing-sensitive: the source documents that VS Code can invoke the hook before its completion event flushes; the capture path does not retry the transcript parse, relying on a later hook call to merge the richer event ([capture_query.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store/config/capture_query.rs#L42-L62)).
+
+## 2. Current test reality
+
+`copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs` has 8 tests. It uses temp directories and either an
+in-process parser call or `Command` against `CARGO_BIN_EXE_copilot-capture-hook`.
+
+| Test | Assertion |
+|---|---|
+| `e2e_parses_fixture_transcript_payload` | Synthetic JSONL yields the expected ID and at least one message. |
+| `e2e_hook_binary_persists_fixture_transcript` | CLI binary persists turns, workspace slug, trigger, and no empty metrics sidecar. |
+| `e2e_hook_binary_populates_tool_metrics_from_captured_tool_events` | Tool start/complete produce one successful `grep_search` call with 1500 ms duration. |
+| `e2e_val_session_api_tool_metrics_gate_asserts_nonempty_tools_map` | A producer-shaped tool transcript produces a nonempty `read_file` metrics map. |
+| `e2e_hook_binary_captures_output_chars_from_hook_stdin_tool_response` | Hook stdin `tool_response` produces payload-sourced nonzero output size. |
+| `e2e_hook_binary_captures_output_chars_from_spill_file_when_hook_payload_empty` | Empty hook payload uses the derived spill file for output size. |
+| `e2e_capture_hook_script_persists_fixture_from_nested_workspace_cwd` | Bash compatibility script invoked from a nested temp workspace persists all three session artifacts. |
+| `e2e_parses_multiple_local_fixture_scenarios` | Each local deterministic scenario parses with a session ID and visible messages. |
+
+The real-binary assertions are visible in [copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs#L57-L176) and the nested-CWD script test in [copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs#L477-L654). The suite does not exercise concurrent processes, file locking/permissions/disk failure, malformed or non-UTF8 stdin/transcripts, the registered `PostToolUse` timing race, the actual VS Code debug-log layout, or full production event metadata.
+
+`copilot_stop_hook_e2e.rs` has 4 tests. It duplicates the parse and binary-persist
+tests (accepting either stop or capture binary), runs the stop compatibility script
+from nested CWD, and scans local fixture scenarios. It likewise uses tempdirs plus
+in-process parsing or a subprocess; it does not add adverse-input, locking,
+concurrency, or recorded-live-data coverage.
+
+`src/hook/tests/capture_request.rs` has 2 in-process unit tests: one maps a
+hand-built `CopilotHookPayload` into a `SessionRecord` and checks links/model/turn
+shape; the other rejects a blank session ID ([capture_request.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/tests/capture_request.rs#L22-L94)). These tests do not parse stdin, read a real JSONL file, invoke the binary, or touch storage.
+
+The existing `capture_hook_workspace_e2e.jsonl` fixture has exactly 3 records: a
+`session.start`, a `user.message`, and an `assistant.message`. It is hand-authored
+synthetic data, not a recorded Copilot artifact: its constant sentence content and
+fixed `session-workspace-fixture` identifier appear directly in the three-line
+fixture ([capture_hook_workspace_e2e.jsonl](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/fixtures/capture_hook_workspace_e2e.jsonl#L1-L3)). It omits event IDs, parent IDs, agent/model/runtime versions, tool execution start/complete events, tool arguments/results, `tool_use_id`, `tool_response`, spill paths, and every full hook-stdin field.
+
+## 3. Real-data recording plan
+
+The requested host path
+`c:/Users/linus/AppData/Roaming/Code/User/workspaceStorage/8c555ca5a1e8e713994831dc7a55167b/GitHub.copilot-chat/debug-logs/`
+was absent from the shell-visible filesystem during this audit; `ls` therefore
+could not provide file sizes or a safe bounded head. This is an evidence limitation,
+not evidence that the VS Code extension never writes logs. Source establishes the
+artifact families required for capture: transcripts at
+`GitHub.copilot-chat/transcripts/<session>.jsonl` and tool spills at
+`chat-session-resources/<session>/<tool_use_id>/content.txt|content.json`
+([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L129-L134), [hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L163-L200)). The actual debug-log format remains undiscoverable on this host.
+
+Recording procedure:
+
+1. Add a local-only wrapper command before the real binary in a developer's VS
+   Code hook config. The wrapper must write a manifest with sanitized argv, selected
+   environment (`PWD`, current directory, no secrets), raw stdin bytes, exit status,
+   stdout/stderr, and timestamps; then pipe the unchanged stdin to the real
+   `copilot-capture-hook --from-hook-stdin`.
+2. After each invocation, copy the referenced transcript and the exact
+   `chat-session-resources/<session>/<tool_use_id>/` directory if present. Record
+   file names, byte counts, and capture ordering; do not rely on a later scan because
+   PostToolUse races the asynchronous spill write.
+3. Create a deterministic sanitization pass that substitutes workspace roots with
+   `<WORKSPACE>`, user/profile paths with `<USER_HOME>`, UUID/session/tool IDs with
+   stable fixture IDs, timestamps with fixed timestamps, and textual prompt,
+   assistant, tool-argument, tool-result, terminal-output, diagnostic, and file
+   content fields with typed synthetic values preserving length/Unicode/newline
+   properties. Remove tokens, credentials, URLs with signed query strings, email,
+   repository remotes, hostnames, and any copied source contents.
+4. Run the hook against the sanitized bundle in CI and assert exact persisted JSON
+   artifacts plus stdout/stderr/exit status.
+
+No existing registered wrapper records argv/stdin/env; registration executes the
+binary directly ([hooks.json](../../.github/hooks/hooks.json#L3-L59)). A legacy
+`tools/agent-hooks/session-capture-stop.sh` exists only as compatibility-script test
+coverage, not as the registered capture command ([copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs#L477-L543)).
+
+Proposed layout:
+
+```text
+memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/fixtures/copilot-capture/
+  README.md
+  post-tool-use-spill-v1/
+    invocation.json
+    stdin.json
+    transcripts/session.jsonl
+    chat-session-resources/session/tool-1__vscode-0/content.txt
+    expected/session.json
+    expected/transcript.json
+    expected/events.json
+    expected/tool-metrics.json
+  stop-minimal-v1/
+    invocation.json
+    stdin.json
+    transcripts/session.jsonl
+    expected/session.json
+```
+
+Privacy rule: commit only fully sanitized, reviewed fixtures. Keep raw recordings
+local, outside the repository, and generate sanitized candidates locally for human
+review. A raw fixture is unsuitable for commit because transcript messages,
+tool arguments/results, resource content, debug logs, and paths can contain prompts,
+source, secrets, or machine identity.
+
+## 4. Proposed test matrix
+
+| Case | Input variation | Expected observable outcome | Currently covered? |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | Valid CLI flags and minimal JSONL | Exit 0, `{}`, session persisted | Y, capture e2e |
+| 2 | Missing `--transcript-path` without stdin mode | Exit 1 and missing-flag stderr | N |
+| 3 | Unknown argv flag | Exit 1 and unknown-argument stderr | N |
+| 4 | `--help` | Usage stdout and exit 0 | N |
+| 5 | Default slug/trigger | Persist `default` and `stop` | N |
+| 6 | Path with spaces | Correct transcript and store resolution | N |
+| 7 | Windows drive-letter path | Correct normalized open on Windows | N |
+| 8 | WSL `/mnt/c/...` path on Windows | Converted path opens | N |
+| 9 | Empty transcript path via stdin | Exit 0, skip stderr, `{}` | N |
+| 10 | Valid hook stdin object | JSON aliases drive capture | Y, nested-CWD e2e |
+| 11 | Empty stdin | Defaults then successful skip | N |
+| 12 | Malformed stdin JSON | Exit 1 with invalid-JSON stderr | N |
+| 13 | stdin JSON array/scalar | Fields ignored, successful skip | N |
+| 14 | Wrong-type `transcript_path` | Field ignored, successful skip | N |
+| 15 | Blank/`null` ordinary stdin fields | Defaults retained | N |
+| 16 | `hook_event_name: unknown` | Persist trigger `stop` | N |
+| 17 | Nonempty `tool_response` | Override terminal event with payload count | Y, capture e2e |
+| 18 | Empty `tool_response` plus spill | Override uses spill count | Y, capture e2e |
+| 19 | Non-UTF8 stdin bytes | Exit 1, no partial store write | N |
+| 20 | Minimal valid transcript | Session ID and visible turns persisted | Y, capture and stop e2e |
+| 21 | Empty JSONL / no messages | Exit 1 `EmptyTurns` | N |
+| 22 | Missing session-start ID | Exit 1 `MissingSessionId` | Y, inline request test only; not parser/binary |
+| 23 | Malformed mid-file JSONL record | Exit 1 and no partial capture | N |
+| 24 | Truncated final JSONL line | Exit 1 and no partial capture | N |
+| 25 | Non-UTF8 transcript bytes | Exit 1 and no partial capture | N |
+| 26 | Oversized transcript/event | Bounded completion and correct capture | N |
+| 27 | Tool start/complete event pair | Metrics include count, success, duration | Y, capture e2e |
+| 28 | Full recorded event metadata and nested subagent IDs | Event fields and attribution survive | N |
+| 29 | Spill appears after PostToolUse starts | Correct later merge or documented no-measurement | N |
+| 30 | Spill absent/unreadable | Capture succeeds; no fabricated output size | N |
+| 31 | `content.json` spill | Character count uses JSON file | N |
+| 32 | Non-UTF8 spill | Lossy character count is persisted | N |
+| 33 | Store root absent | Directories and artifacts created | N |
+| 34 | Session files read-only/locked | Exit 1, prior artifacts intact | N |
+| 35 | Disk-full-style temp-write/rename failure | Exit 1, prior artifacts intact, temp cleanup assessed | N |
+| 36 | Two concurrent invocations, same session | No lost events/turns and valid JSON artifacts | N |
+| 37 | Two concurrent invocations, different sessions | Independent valid artifacts | N |
+| 38 | Repeated triggers after transcript grows | Merge is idempotent and richer event retained | N |
+
+Matrix total: 38 cases; 7 are currently covered at the stated observable level and
+31 are uncovered. The inline blank-session-ID test is useful unit coverage but does
+not validate the parser/binary contract, so case 22 remains untested end-to-end.
+
+## 5. Root-cause read
+
+The requested command, `git log --oneline -- memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs memory-api/crates/session-api/src/hook/ | head -40`, and the equivalent `--all` command returned no entries in this checkout. Accordingly, commit-level past fixes and commit hashes are unavailable; claiming a history-derived list would be unsupported.
+
+Source comments and regression test names nevertheless identify three recurring
+failure themes that the new suite must protect:
+
+| Failure theme | Source evidence | Matrix recurrence guard |
+|---|---|---|
+| Real producer tool telemetry differs from hand-constructed tool turns | Existing regression commentary says real Copilot has no `role: Tool` turns and requires event replay ([copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/tests/copilot_capture_hook_e2e.rs#L178-L184)). | 27, 28 |
+| PostToolUse output is empty or races asynchronous spill/transcript writes | The hook explicitly falls back from `tool_response` to a spill file and retries its discovery; the capture path documents a missing completion event at fire time ([hook.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook.rs#L135-L200); [capture_query.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/store/config/capture_query.rs#L42-L62)). | 17, 18, 29, 30, 31, 32, 38 |
+| Workspace/CWD and platform path resolution diverge from the test process | Default roots use working directory/PWD; the test suite needed a nested-CWD script regression, and Windows has WSL-path conversion ([workspace.rs](../../memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/workspace.rs#L108-L113); [args.rs](../../memory-api/crates/session-api/src/bin/copilot-capture-hook/args.rs#L145-L197)). | 6, 7, 8, 10, 33 |
+
+Strongest recommendation: add one fully sanitized recorded PostToolUse bundle plus a
+fixture harness that replays stdin, transcript, and spill resources through the real
+binary, then add a two-process same-session contention test. That pair targets the
+largest live-environment mismatch and the unaudited read/merge/write race.
*** End Patch

turns.content: The evidence set is sufficient for a bounded first-pass inventory: Rust tests dominate, fixture-backed integration is present, and no `proptest`, `quickcheck`, `arbitrary`, or `insta` test dependencies were found; Criterion appears only as benchmark infrastructure. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import os,subprocess,re,sys,json
root='c:/Users/linus/git/context-engine'
crates=[
  'memory-api/crates/memory-api',
  'memory-api/crates/spec-api',
  'memory-api/crates/test-api',
  'memory-api/crates/peek-api',
  'memory-api/crates/feedback-api',
  'memory-api/crates/doc-api',
  'memory-api/crates/audit-api',
  'memory-api/crates/fs-api',
  'memory-api/crates/rule-api',
  'memory-api/crates/compact-terminal-api',
  'memory-api/crates/memory-matrix',
  'memory-api/crates/memory-fixtures',
  'memory-api/crates/ticket',
  'context-stack/context-api',
  'context-stack/context-read',
  'context-stack/context-trace-macros',
  'memory-viewers/spec-viewer',
  'memory-viewers/doc-viewer',
]
results=[]
for c in crates:
    path=os.path.join(root,c)
    if not os.path.isdir(path):
        results.append({'crate':c,'loc':0,'cfg_files':0,'test_attrs':0,'tests_dir_files':0,'benches':0,'examples':0,'desc':'MISSING'})
        continue
    # git ls-files for this crate
    try:
        out=subprocess.check_output(['git','ls-files',c],cwd=root,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).decode('utf-8')
        files=[p for p in out.splitlines() if p.endswith('.rs')]
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        files=[]
    loc=0
    for f in files:
        fp=os.path.join(root,f)
        try:
            with open(fp,'rb') as fh:
                # count lines
                loc += sum(1 for _ in fh)
        except Exception:
            pass
    # cfg test files count (files under src that contain #[cfg(test)])
    cfg_files=0
    src_dir=os.path.join(path,'src')
    if os.path.isdir(src_dir):
        for dirpath,_,filenames in os.walk(src_dir):
            for fn in filenames:
                if not fn.endswith('.rs'): continue
                fp=os.path.join(dirpath,fn)
                try:
                    s=open(fp,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
                except Exception:
                    s=''
                if '#[cfg(test)]' in s:
                    cfg_files += 1
    # test attrs count anywhere in crate
    test_attrs=0
    pattern=re.compile(r'#\[(?:tokio::test|test)\]')
    for dirpath,_,filenames in os.walk(path):
        for fn in filenames:
            if not fn.endswith('.rs'): continue
            fp=os.path.join(dirpath,fn)
            try:
                s=open(fp,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
            except Exception:
                s=''
            test_attrs += len(pattern.findall(s))
    # tests dir files
    tests_dir_files=0
    tdir=os.path.join(path,'tests')
    if os.path.isdir(tdir):
        tests_dir_files = len([n for n in os.listdir(tdir) if n.endswith('.rs')])
    benches=0
    bdir=os.path.join(path,'benches')
    if os.path.isdir(bdir):
        benches = len([n for n in os.listdir(bdir) if n.endswith('.rs')])
    examples=0
    edir=os.path.join(path,'examples')
    if os.path.isdir(edir):
        examples = len([n for n in os.listdir(edir) if n.endswith('.rs')])
    # description
    desc=''
    ct=os.path.join(path,'Cargo.toml')
    if os.path.isfile(ct):
        try:
            s=open(ct,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
            m=re.search(r'^description\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"',s,flags=re.MULTILINE)
            if m:
                desc=m.group(1)
        except Exception:
            desc=''
    if not desc:
        lib=os.path.join(path,'src','lib.rs')
        if os.path.isfile(lib):
            try:
                s=open(lib,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore').read()
                m=re.search(r'^//!\s*(.+)',s,flags=re.MULTILINE)
                if m:
                    desc=m.group(1).strip()
            except Exception:
                desc=''
    results.append({'crate':c,'loc':loc,'cfg_files':cfg_files,'test_attrs':test_attrs,'tests_dir_files':tests_dir_files,'benches':benches,'examples':examples,'desc':desc})
# write markdown as requested
out_md=os.path.join(root,'tmp','test-coverage-audit','01b-coverage-verification.md')
with open(out_md,'w',encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('# Coverage verification\n\n')
    f.write('## Section 1 — Verdict table\n\n')
    f.write('crate | src LOC | inline #[cfg(test)] files | total #[test]/#[tokio::test] count | tests/ dir file count | benches/ | VERDICT\n')
    f.write('---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---\n')
    for r in results:
        verdict = 'CONFIRMED ZERO' if (r['cfg_files']==0 and r['test_attrs']==0 and r['tests_dir_files']==0) else 'REFUTED'

[02 §1, §4](02-code-surface.md) [02b §2-3](02b-code-surface-addendum.md)

questions.question: Spec 1d62442b says "CLI commands should produce compact output by default." What is the default, and is its byte size capped?
questions.message:
**Entity:** spec `1d62442b` — ticket-api state transition path unification.

**Current text:** "CLI commands should produce compact output by default; use `--verbose` or `--json` only when needed."

**Undetermined:** what "compact" means concretely, and whether output is golden-testable.

**Consequences:**
- **A** lets us write byte-exact golden tests, but every cosmetic output tweak becomes a breaking change requiring fixture updates.
- **B** tests field *presence and values* without freezing layout — resilient to presentation changes, weaker at catching accidental verbosity regressions.
- **C** is the most automation-friendly and simplest to assert, but changes human UX for every CLI in the repo.

options.label: A — Human text default, defined fields + byte cap (golden-testable)
options.description: Strongest tests; presentation changes become breaking

options.label: B — Human text default, stable field presence, no byte cap
options.description: Presentation may evolve; assert semantics only

options.label: C — JSON becomes the default output for all CLIs
options.description: Best for automation; changes human UX everywhere

questions.question: Spec 1d62442b says HTTP and MCP "should support both TOON and JSON, with TOON as the recommended default." How is format selected, and what happens on an invalid selector?
questions.message:
**Entity:** spec `1d62442b`.

**Current text:** "HTTP and MCP endpoints should support both TOON and JSON, with TOON as the recommended default for agent-to-agent communication."

**Undetermined:** the selector mechanism, the actual default, the response content type, and the invalid-selector error.

**Consequences:**
- **A** gives one parity matrix testable identically across HTTP and MCP; TOON default saves agent tokens but surprises HTTP clients expecting JSON.
- **B** is least surprising for standard HTTP tooling and simplest to document; agents must opt in every call.
- **C** matches current behavior most closely but forces a per-transport exception table, roughly doubling parity test cases.

Note: whichever you pick, I will also need the invalid-selector behavior pinned (HTTP 406 vs 400 vs silent JSON fallback) — say so in freeform if you have a preference.

options.label: A — Explicit selector (Accept header / request field), TOON default
options.description: One rule both transports; agent-token optimized

options.label: B — JSON default, TOON strictly opt-in
options.description: Least surprising for HTTP clients

options.label: C — Per-transport defaults, documented exception table
options.description: Closest to today; doubles parity test cases

questions.question: Spec 58a1d32c claims canonical paths close TOCTOU windows. What symlink behavior must fs-api/fs-cli/fs-mcp actually guarantee?
questions.message:
**Entity:** spec `58a1d32c` — filesystem operations: bounded listing, stat, and conflict-aware mutation.

**Current text:** "All `std::fs::*` calls operate on the canonical path returned by `validate_path_within_root()`, closing TOCTOU windows."

**Undetermined:** the supported adversary model. This is a **security contract**, so guessing it encodes the wrong guarantee — hence the escalation.

**Consequences:**
- **A** is the strongest guarantee and easiest to assert, but breaks any legitimate in-root symlink usage.
- **B** is the usual practical policy; tests must cover symlink-escape *and* symlink-resolves-inside cases, and race-window behavior on Windows vs Unix differs and must be pinned per platform.
- **C** means we must stop advertising TOCTOU protection, and security tests become non-assertions.

options.label: A — Reject all symlink traversal inside the root
options.description: Strongest, simplest to test; breaks in-root symlinks

options.label: B — Permit symlinks that resolve inside the root, reject escapes
options.description: Practical; needs per-platform race tests

options.label: C — Document as best-effort, drop the TOCTOU claim
options.description: Honest but removes a security guarantee

questions.question: feedback-cli and feedback-mcp are public contracts with NO behavior spec and NO validation spec. How should the feedback contract be specified?
questions.message:

questions.message:
**Entity:** spec `39983ddf` — Model price awareness, implemented by `memory-api/tools/mcp/mcp-toolmon`.

**Current text:** "expensive-model calls to token-heavy tools refused with delegation guidance; cheap-model calls pass unchanged."

**Undetermined:** what counts as expensive, what counts as token-heavy, and whether the outcome is a hard refusal or advice.

**Note the tension:** `.agents/instructions/orchestration/model-prices.instructions.md` states "No model is ever denied outright" and describes a *graded budget*, which contradicts the spec's word "refused." One of the two is wrong and the tests will encode whichever you pick.

**Consequences:**
- **A** is trivially testable with fixed cases but goes stale whenever prices move.
- **B** matches the graded-budget design already implemented and keeps prices out of code; tests must assert the *formula*, not magic numbers.
- **C** resolves the contradiction toward the instruction file, but weakens the gate to guidance only.

options.description: Trivially testable; goes stale as prices change

options.label: B — Compute from a versioned policy table (graded budget)
options.description: Matches implemented design; assert the formula

questions.message:
**Entity:** spec `9f0b9e30` — caller_model resolution semantics for the MCP cost gate.

**Why you are being asked:** I attempted this as a mechanical sharpening. The agent found spec `9f0b9e30` defines **neither** a concrete `N` **nor** an ordering comparator, so applying it would have invented a contract. It was left untouched and escalated — it is the one item blocking branch `agent/specsharp-spec-sharpening` from being fully complete.

**Undetermined:** the numeric cap and the deterministic ordering.

**Consequences:** ordering must be *deterministic* whatever you choose, otherwise the error message cannot be asserted at all. Alphabetical is the cheapest to test; cheapest-first is the most useful to an agent being told to delegate; nearest-match is the most helpful for typos but needs a distance function pinned too.

options.label: N=5, cheapest-first by output_mtok
options.description: Doubles as delegation guidance

options.label: N=10, nearest-match by edit distance to the input

event_meta.reasoning_text:
I've consolidated all thirteen decisions and now I'm materializing the ticket epic. The key points are: CLI outputs TOON by default with stable field presence and no byte cap, validating both semantics and format; transport negotiation defaults to JSON for HTTP and TOON for MCP with explicit selectors available; and I'm working through the filesystem adversary model considerations.

Continuing through the remaining decisions: the feedback contract uses a single shared API spec across CLI and MCP transports, cost gating employs a versioned policy table with graded budgets, and rejection guidance returns five candidates—not-found errors suggest nearest matches by edit distance, while too-expensive errors recommend viable models by highest tier first then cheapest within that tier. Session guards require valid session IDs for specific tool calls via mcp-toolmon as a pre-tool hook, concurrent check-ins use a lease/access model where the orchestrator claims leases on ticket tracks and worktrees with auto-release on session finish, and I'm establishing a strict field parity matrix across CLI, MCP, and HTTP transports with performance targets based on hardware classification.

The browser preference decision moves to contributor policy in the instructions, graph traversal needs exact flags with BFS semantics including depth and cycle handling, and TOON docs should generate examples from command schemas with validation of the output. Items 7 and 8 represent substantial new designs requiring their own spec and implementation tickets rather than just test coverage. Now I'm designing the epic structure as a mutation to the ticket store—this is my orchestrator decomposition job, starting with a Phase 1 contract refinement phase that blocks most other work.

I'm applying the batch interview decisions across those eight specs, authoring the shared feedback-api spec that currently lacks definition, moving the browser preference spec to the agents instructions, and creating two new specs: one for the session-scoped access-lease model with inheritance and auto-release hooks, and another for mcp-toolmon as a session-guard pre-tool hook.

I also need to publish the CLI/MCP/HTTP parity matrix as a machine-readable artifact and merge the pending spec-sharpening branch that's already been committed with five edits.

For the test foundation phase, I'm setting up fixture sanitization with a directory convention, building multi-store sandbox and replay harness helpers, and introducing property-based testing with proptest since there's currently none in the repo. The capture hook phase focuses on recording and sanitizing real PostToolUse/Stop events to close the largest gap in the matrix coverage.

Next I'm implementing replay tests for the 31 uncovered matrix rows and adding concurrency, contention, and write-failure tests. The transport matrices phase tackles the highest-risk surfaces: parity tests across CLI/MCP/HTTP for tickets and sessions, graph traversal semantics including cycle handling, and output format validation across TOON CLI, MCP TOON, HTTP JSON, and selector modes. After that I'll move through the remaining surfaces starting with the filesystem layer. Phase 7 wraps up with recurring audit templates, guidance on writing good tests, and evaluating coverage tooling like cargo-llvm-cov. That's roughly 28 tickets across the epic, which is substantial but matches what was requested for a multi-phase interview and testing initiative. Now I need to dispatch ticket creation—this modifies the .ticket file, which is separate from the .spec changes, so I should consider whether to use a worktree to keep things clean and avoid merge conflicts. Ticket creation is a store operation, not code work, so I should do it at root rather than fragmenting across worktrees — that's what causes merge conflicts. The spec-sharpening branch is ready to merge, and I should probably apply the escalated fix first before merging.

Actually, I'll merge the branch as-is with its five clean sharpenings, then fold the escalated decision into ticket T1.1 where it belongs. I can dispatch two agents in parallel: one to merge the spec-sharpening branch and clean up the worktree, and another to create the ticket epic.

Agent B's job is substantial—29 tickets with descriptions and dependencies—so I'll assign that to Terra. But I need to check my ticket tooling first: looking at the mcp_ticket-mcp capabilities, I see I can update and close tickets, but I don't see a direct create_ticket function in the available tools.

However, sub-agents likely have access to more tools. The ticket-cli has a batch command that can handle transactional ticket creation, so I'll instruct the agent to use `ticket batch` and check the help docs for the right format. I'll also need to handle dependencies through `ticket link` and verify the valid edge kinds by checking `list_edges`.

Let me write out the full epic spec for Agent B with the complete tree structure inline so it doesn't need to design it from scratch, and I'll include the decisions record so the tickets carry that context. Then I'll dispatch both agents.
